utterances.text: Mr. President, I can actually move on. I can move on to a new area. If the witness could be provided, please, with Prosecutor's Exhibit 777 and also if you could have Defence Exhibit 142 available.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: General, this is not an order that you have seen before, and I'm not particularly concerned with the content. I'm more concerned with the format.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if you could place that on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: General, you're a senior military man. Is it normal in an order from a battalion for the title of the unit, stated here "5th Engineers Battalion Command," to be incorporated into the form of the order? Is that standard practice?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand your question, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you look in the top, left-hand corner of this order, you will see that it states "5th Engineers Battalion Command," and then it states the location, "Konjevic Polje," and then it states the number of the order, "9-4/94," and it also incorporates the date. You were a commander of a battalion. Is it standard practice for an order to be set out in this format?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the type of official correspondence. If it is open post, that is to say sent by regular post, then the communication is with the military post, and here 50/60/1. Then in the register they know what unit it concerns. If it is a confidential post and if the way in which it is dispatched is confidential and controlled, then this is the manner in which the communication is made.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Would an order always contain the name of the unit and the number of the order?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it refers to an order from a superior, then it would be customary for the number to be mentioned, or if there is no mention of any number, then mention is made of what the order refers to. For example, pursuant to the order on the transfer of the soldier of such-and-such a date, in that case, you don't have to have a number. But it is customary for a number to exist. That is the must customary mode of procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown Defence Exhibit 142.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We've nearly finished, General. Now, General, you'll see that this is an order in the same format as the previous one that we've seen, but it is, in fact, missing the name of the command and the order number. Would this order have had those markings on them in its original form? Would it have had the "Command of the 5th Engineering Battalion" and the file number on the original document?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you just give me a moment to read through the order to see what it is about, because depending on what the order contains will depend how the document is -- the appearance of the document. Yes. I think I can answer now. This order has a series of omissions. There are a series of omissions. First of all, he orders that he will be replaced by his deputy. The deputy replaces or stands in by definition, so there would be no reason for this to be stated. This is a document for internal command, that is to say, it just makes public in the unit that this man will be standing in. His order on this standing in does not lead to the same kind of consequences as would a document received from the Superior Command. No personal rights from the service does this stand-in for the commander have on the basis of this type of document. Had the Superior Command compiled this document, the person taking over the function would have the right to higher salaries, more rights, perhaps the right to an apartment and so on, which goes with the post, with the function. But this kind of paper, this document, only has the function of informing that he will be replacing him and that he won't be in the unit at that specific time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: General, don't you think it's unusual that this order makes no reference in the form of a caption like the last order to the 5th Engineers Battalion command and to the order number? There is no reference on this document to the order number at all. Don't you think that's unusual?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that this is an internal document. It's just a document within the unit, an internal one. So the person compiling this document did not do what you said, and that is an omission, a mistake of this document. It wasn't shaped properly. But even if it were, the results would be no different.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We can move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: General, do you recall in your evidence you stated, and this is at page 8051: "If, in the command system and the system of informing, the Command of the Drina Corps found out that these units committed something that was proscribed under regulations, then they would be obliged, the Drina Corps, and the command system would be obliged to act in accordance or exactly the same way that any officer or any member of an army would behave when they found out that somebody was acting against rules and regulations, meaning that procedures would have to be initiated and investigations which would be required in such a particular case. So only in this regard can there be responsibility for the conduct of others in their zone."

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, General, are you aware that General Krstic has stated to this Court that he was informed about what happened in the Drina Corps zone in late August? Are you aware of that, that he was aware of all of the executions, of everything that had happened, in late August? I'm sorry, I'll correct that. He was aware of a number of executions in the corps area of responsibility by late August; are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, I'm acquainted with General Krstic's statement, what he said was that he learnt of the executions when he returned to the command post, which means that that was -- that before the end of the operation, he did not know about it, if I got the meaning of your question properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: General, General Krstic has stated that by late August, he was aware of executions that had happened in the Corps zone of responsibility. Are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Now, based on your theory that you presented to the Court, that there is an obligation on all VRS officers to do something about alleged atrocities, even if the unit is not one of your own, General Krstic had an obligation to do something about these crimes that had happened within his area of responsibility, didn't he, General?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Finally, General, I want to refer to a section of your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And this is page 66 in the English version, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And page 66 in your version, General. It's paragraph 4.3. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: It's page 66, Mr. Usher, paragraph 4.3.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And it's the section that begins "Goran Matic," and I'll read it. "Goran Matic, the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia Information Minister, talked about the massacre of Muslim civilians at a press conference when giving information about results of the investigation conducted against the arrested "Pauk" (or Spider) group. That group consisted of paid Croats, Slovenes, Muslims, and Serbs. French intelligence service organised, equipped, and trained the group to perform the massacre of Muslim civilians with the aim of attributing that crime to the Serbs and declaring the Serb military and political strategy to be criminal and Republika Srpska as a political result of a world crime. After that scenario, all violence against the Serbs became legitimate." Paragraph 4.4: "Neither General Krstic nor any other Serb commanding officer could have known about that criminal plan, and so unfortunately they could," and it says "could prevent," I believe you meant they "could not" prevent it. General, do you really believe that the French intelligence services used mercenaries to kill thousands of Muslims in the Zvornik and Bratunac areas in July of 1995? Do you believe that statement by Goran Matic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I, as a responsible individual, with a difficult subject to study which is pregnant with terrible crimes over which there is a great deal of controversy, I did not consider that I had the right to ignore the fact that before the national public and the international public, the authorised representative of any country whatsoever should present facts and presented facts about the participation of a group of people which at that point in time was under the control of the Yugoslav legal system and Yugoslav courts, and as the direct --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: General, do you believe that Goran Matic was telling the truth? It's in your report, General. You refer to this. Was Goran Matic telling the truth when he said the French intelligence services were responsible for killing of thousands of people in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I do not know or not know [as interpreted] whether he was telling the truth. And as somebody that studied the topic, I could not ignore the fact that that minister at that time spoke about that subject. Therefore, I included it in my expert report without giving it too much specific weight, but just indicating the fact, pointing this fact out, because maybe that had an effect on the events that took place as well. And that I was not totally wrong is borne out by the decision of the French parliament to form an investigative commission about that matter. I don't think that I influenced this, or the Yugoslav minister either, but most probably the facts that became known and the intention to have openly -- and precisely locate the events and perpetrators. So my quotation and what I say goes along those lines. It is not arbitration one way or another, either for or against. It is a presentation of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: General, thank you very much indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, thank you. I've finished my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Cayley, thank you. Mr. Visnjic, do you have additional questions to pose to the witness? Shall we take a break, depending on how much time you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I do have some questions, but I should welcome a break because we're going to use some exhibits, and perhaps it would be opportune to take a rather longer break so that we can put all that in order. Thank you, Mr. President. I don't think I will need more than 40 minutes, one hour to the most, for my additional examination of the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is now more or less time for our long break of the day. So shall we have a 20-minute -- if we have a 20-minute break, we'll have to interrupt for the lunch break, or shall we take the lunch break now? Perhaps that would be better. Yes? I see that there is general acquiescence and support for the latter proposal for the lunch break. Perhaps lunch isn't ready yet, but anyway, that's why I was wondering, but let us take a 50-minute lunch break. --- Luncheon recess taken at 11.51 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Visnjic. You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask the usher to show the witness Prosecution Exhibit 425, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, would you be kind enough to find - this is directive 7 - the part related to the obligation to inform. It is toward the end. Actually, it's the last page.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: My learned friend Mr. Cayley, in the cross-examination, asked you about the obligation to inform units as envisaged in this directive, and you answered his questions. My question is the following: Have you found in the course of your research any report or any response addressed by a unit to the Main Staff or the Supreme Commander directly linked to the order in the directive?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not come across any such document. It would have been natural for the Main Staff of the VRS to inform the commands of the operations assigned to them and Commander of the Drina Corps and the Drina Corps Commands, their Main Staff about the operations assigned to them. So I have not come across any such document, and my conclusion is that this is because those operations were mostly not conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General Radinovic, if the directive number 7 had been implemented, would the plan for the Srebrenica operation been called Krivaja 95?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the directive number 7 had been applied, then the plan of the operation for Srebrenica would not have been called Krivaja 95 because directive number 7, Krivaja -- the code name Krivaja was meant for the Hercegovina Corps in the far south of Republika Srpska, and it was planned that this operation be conducted in the Neretva River valley, which is a completely different part of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Let me go on to another topic now. I'm referring to the period of the 12th and the 13th and the situation in Potocari. The Prosecution asked you about the involvement of two or four officers of the Drina Corps in this operation, and the question was whether one could conclude that the Drina Corps conducted the operation. Let me put a hypothetical to you. If two or several officers of the Main Staff took part in the operation of the displacement of the population from Potocari to Tuzla, that is, if two or more officers were sighted on the spot or two or more officers engaged in active engagement within the framework of that operation, would you agree with the submission that the Main Staff was in charge of the operation?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree with that statement because the presence of officers of the Main Staff, including the Main Staff commander, is a sign that the operation was conducted by the Main Staff, a very significant sign, and the fact that resources of the Drina Corps were included is quite natural because the Main Staff is not an abstract concept. It is using the effectives of the VRS available to it in particular areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask the usher to show the witness Prosecution Exhibit 77/6.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General Radinovic, could you please look at the second sentence of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would read it in English so the interpreters can interpret it for the General. The second sentence. Could the exhibit be moved down a little.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Visnjic, excuse me. Which exhibit are we looking at? It says 77/6, but I am told by the interpreters that they heard a different exhibit number. Which exhibit are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is Prosecution Exhibit OTP 77/6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General Radinovic, allow me to read the second sentence of this report, and then I will ask you a question related to it. [In English] "UNMOs have so far counted up to 31 explosions in Potocari but due to the distance, there may be more that we have not heard." [Interpretation] General Radinovic, in this Trial Chamber, two Defence witnesses have testified, Witness DC and Witness Borovcanin. According to the testimony of Witness DC, to be found on pages 7441 and 7442 of the transcript, on a number of occasions -- and I will paraphrase the witness who said that she heard artillery fire but of a very limited amount, and focussing most on Muslim bunkers. The other witness, Borovcanin, spoke about this on ten pages of the transcript, pages 7001 and 7 -- from 7001 to 7022 -- 7011, 7022. Allow me to repeat it once again for the transcript. I see it's correct now: from pages 7011 to page 7022. The witness also said that he heard explosions occasionally, that they were not numerous, that he also heard occasional detonations. And also in a part of his testimony he said that the shelling was few and far between, even when he got quite close to the town, and that was on the 10th, and he was at a distance of some two kilometres as the crow flies. Through your cross-examination by the Prosecution, we referred to the number of explosions on the basis of a variety of reports shown to you by the Prosecution. My question is the following: What would be your comment to the fact that both UN observers and members of the VRS come to the same conclusion; that there is a possibility that they may not have heard everything that was used, that was caused by artillery shelling, and in that context, which reports do you have the greatest faith in?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that it is possible for members of the VRS not to have heard all the explosions in the broader area of Srebrenica, especially if those witnesses learnt about the number of explosions from one particular location. The causes can be different. There may be an obstacle in front of them in the direction from which the shelling can be heard, then the sound is pushed back. If they were so far away that an explosion could not be heard, that could be a reason, too. And also, the same could apply to UN observers who were in the urban part of the area. And as you know, the operation was being conducted on the whole area, that is, the whole breadth of the enclave, wherever there were positions held by members of the 28th Division, and the only people who could, with relative reliability, identify the explosions were members of the Dutch Battalion who were at their observation posts. And as I have testified here, the number of those identified explosions by the Dutch Battalion are considerably higher than the figures given by the UNMOs. I think that the UN monitors mention a figure of 870 Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. or 780, I'm not sure which, whereas members of the Dutch Battalion talk about a number of 1.338. So the difference is quite considerable. So I am confident that the members of the Dutch Battalion provided much more precise figures, and I am prone to trust those rather than those given by the members of the VRS and members of the United Nations monitors.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Does the strength of the explosion depend on the artillery being used? In other words, a higher calibre weapon would produce a more powerful sound?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. I'm not an expert for artillery shells, but being a member of the Engineers, and I have dealt with explosives, more explosives and a higher calibre produces a louder explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Did members of the Dutch Battalion analyse the structure of the explosions, where they came from, which artillery pieces were used, and so on?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Members of the Dutch Battalion approached the matter in an extremely professional manner, and they reported on the number of explosions, but you didn't go into any analysis as they were not -- they did not study the craters, the ranges, the locations from which the fire came. They didn't analyse the structure of those explosions, but they simply registered the explosions themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General Radinovic, the Prosecutor has made a submission that General Krstic became commander on the 13th of July, 1995. How does the fact that the Chief of Staff - the new Chief of Staff, Colonel Andric, did not take over duty at that time but remained Brigade Commander until the end of the Zepa activities - fit into that theory?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is an eloquent example how documents on appointments cannot and mustn't be interpreted literally. Colonel Andric, the Commander of the Birac Brigade at the time of the Zepa operation, was the Brigade Commander when the appointment came for the Chief of Staff of the Drina Corps, but he did not leave his position as Brigade Commander but remained in that position until the end of the operation and only then took over the duties of Chief of Staff of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General Radinovic, the Prosecutor has also made a contention that the record on the takeover of duty is dated the 13th of July. What is your comment?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would be able to answer your question with precision if I had that report. As, unfortunately, I don't have it, I can only rely on undeniable arguments, and those are that the president of Republika Srpska, in his capacity as Supreme Commander of the VRS, issued a decree on the appointment of General Krstic to the position of Commander of the Drina Corps. This decree is dated the 14th of July and it explicitly issues the order that this should be on the 15th, and there is no army in the world that would ignore the decree on appointment by its Supreme Commander and organise the actual takeover of duty and report on the same two days prior to the date mentioned in the decree. In the report on the handing over of duty and in the preamble of any document, all documents, reference is made to the act pursuant to which this is being done. The handing over of duty is being done by the decree issued by the president of the Republic, issued by the Supreme Commander. How can a report be made referring to a document dated the 14th and the actual transfer of duty to have been signed on the 13th? This is something that cannot be found anywhere in practice, and according to doctrine, that is explicitly prohibited.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 469, and at the same time could you prepare Exhibits - this is a large group but we'll be through with them very quickly - 759, Prosecution Exhibit; Defence Exhibits 76, 96, 77, 78, 98, and Prosecution Exhibits 404/441 and 404/381.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General Radinovic, you have before you an OTP exhibit. I think this is an accompanying document but not the document itself. It must be here somewhere. General Radinovic, I think my learned friend Mr. Cayley asked you whether in the period following the 15th, the 20th, or on some other date, whether there is any information that General Zivanovic held a different post, and you said that you have no such information. My question is: In the period from the 15th to the 20th, if there is no information that General Zivanovic did assume another position, why is that so?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only reason why General Zivanovic could not assume any other position was that the position of Corps Commander is an obligation until he hands over that duty to the newly-appointed commander. Since in the period from the 15th to the 20th that appointment could not have been carried out and it was carried out on the 20th, until then, General Zivanovic cannot be appointed to any other position except the position of Drina Corps Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask the usher now to prepare for the witness, could you prepare for the witness this set of documents that I have just listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General Radinovic, before this document is removed, let me remind you of a part of your answer in response to a question regarding the numbers on the documents and to what extent those numbers are important for identifying who the author of the document is, that is, who is issuing the order.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While they're preparing the documents, so as not to waste time, I understand your question --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: No, let's wait. Perhaps it's better to wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we begin with Exhibit 759, OTP Exhibit. Please take my copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General Radinovic, we're dealing with two documents, and explaining the right half of this exhibit, Exhibit 463, you explained that the number in the heading --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher push the document down a little. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: You explained that the number at the top of the document can identify the commander. Would you please now look at the left half of this same exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher put it onto ELMO. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General Radinovic, who was the commander of the Drina Corps on the 12th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major-General Milenko Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask the usher to place on the ELMO exhibit, Defence Exhibit D76. Could the usher move the document down a little, please, so that we can see the heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General Radinovic, who was the commander of the Drina Corps on the 5th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milenko Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: On the basis of the number of this document, is it possible to ascertain that it was issued by the commander?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher place on the ELMO Exhibit D77, [In English] 77. [Interpretation] Mr. President -- oh, here it is. It's all right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Could I just ask? How could you ascertain that it is issued by the commander? Are there some methods or means, or is it supposed to be evident that if it's there in the name of the commander, it is issued by the commander?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the heading in the left-hand corner of the document, top left-hand corner, there is an indication of the unit and which command system is issuing the document: the Drina Corps command, referring to a particular number, a date, who it is addressed to, the content of the document, and in the lower -- in the bottom corner, the signature, the title and the signature. Among the documents we have seen so far, there was a series issued by the commander without any numerical indication in the top left-hand corner that accompanies that position. As I have already testified, documents issued by the commander should customarily bear the number "01," the Chief of Staff and Deputy Commander "02." That is how those positions are numbered, right down to number 12. But obviously they're not abiding by that convention, and that identification in itself, numerical identification, is not sufficient to establish who authored that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General Radinovic, you have before you Defence Exhibit 77.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could it be moved down so we can see the number in the left-hand corner, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: It is a document issued by the Drina Corps command, forward command post Pribicevac, number 08/95. Who was Chief of Staff of the Drina Corps on the 6th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the benefit of Their Honours, could the English translation of this document be moved up so that we can see who signed it. In the bottom left-hand corner, it is stated "Chief of Staff, Major General Radislav Krstic." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is Exhibit 404, footnote 441, but it is an attachment to the report of Mr. Butler.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Thank you very much.

utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General Radinovic, this is a regular combat report of the Zvornik Brigade, dated the 24th of July, 1995. Who was the Commander of the Zvornik Brigade on the 24th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: On the basis of the numerical indication at the top of this document, if we ignore its content, is it possible to conclude that this was a document issued by the Zvornik Brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher place on the ELMO the last page of this document, please. The last page of the same document. Perhaps we can find the version in Serbian. On the last page, we see the signature of the commander, Lieutenant Colonel Vinko Pandurevic. Could the usher now place on the ELMO Defence Exhibit D78. Mr. President, Your Honours, I have only two more exhibits to show the witness very briefly. These are just examples of a large number of documents that we have in our possession, but we have selected only a few by way of an example.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General Radinovic, the document is on the ELMO now. It is the document issued by the Drina Corps with the number 04/156-5. Who was the Commander of the Drina Corps on the 8th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major-General Milenko Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: On the basis of the numerical indication on this document, can it be inferred that it was issued by the commander of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher now please move the document on the ELMO so we can see the bottom half and the signatory. In the lower left-hand corner, we see "Commander, Major-General Milenko Zivanovic." Could the usher place on the ELMO Prosecution Exhibit -- no. Sorry. Defence Exhibit D98.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Excuse me. Was there any signature on this document of General Zivanovic? I didn't see any signature. Has the original got a signature?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The signature is on the Serbian version. On the Serbian version of the document, there is the signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Is his signature known? Was it -- if this was a forgery, would it be known?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Was there any verification to know it was his signature or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can just inform the Trial Chamber that these are documents on which there is stipulation between the Defence and the Prosecution that they are authentic, and some of the documents are Prosecution exhibits, which is something I omitted to say, and also the Defence had no query as to their authenticity. So now we're talking about Defence Exhibit D98. The Serbian version for the General.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, I must ask you to read first who issued this document and the number under which it is registered, as I don't have a copy with me now.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document was issued by the Commander of the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska on the 11th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And under which number has it been registered?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Strictly confidential number: 03/4-1616."

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General Radinovic, looking at this document, without entering into its content, can you conclude that it was issued by the Commander of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Main Staff of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the number in the left-hand corner, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General Radinovic, who was the Commander of the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska on the 11th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask the usher to find the last page of this document in the English version and to place it on the ELMO. In the bottom left-hand corner, we see the signature of the author of the document, "Commander General Ratko Mladic." Thank you. And that brings to an end this series of documents. I should now like to ask the witness to be shown OTP Exhibit 467. Prosecution Exhibit 467, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General Radinovic, we have before us a document sent by the Command of the 1st Bratunac Brigade, signed by Colonel Vinko Blagojevic. Of course, this document too -- Vidoje Blagojevic. Yes, Vidoje Blagojevic. Of course, this document too has a number. It is 03, which does not denote the commander, but that is not what I want to ask you. What I want to ask you is the following --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpetation] I think the document's well placed on the ELMO now. Leave it like that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Could you comment on this document in the sense of its form and contents, the form and contents of this document. May we have your comments to that, please?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is a report from the commander of the 1st Bratunac Brigade to the command of the Drina Corps in reference to a document which the command of the Drina Corps -- in which it is checking out when the command of the Bratunac Brigade, or rather, its commander is able to attend the handing over and takeover of duties at the command of the Drina Corps. In the heading, we see the date, the 14th of July, the 14th of July 1995. And in the contents of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General Radinovic, just a moment, please. May I interrupt you?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the English version, the date in the top corner is the 17th of July. As the Trial Chamber has already been informed, this is an error on the typewritten page on the document in front of you. So the document was issued on the 14th of July, but on the document, it was typewritten that it was issued on the 17th of July.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I wish to draw attention to a more serious mistake, and that is that, in the response by the commander of the Bratunac Brigade to the command of the Drina Corps, it says that the commander of the brigade will be able to attend the handing over of duty between the old and new command of the Drina Corps on the 23rd of June, on the 23rd of June, 1995. So that is a complete mix-up in the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, what is the probative value, that is to say, how did you -- how do you assess the weight of that document with respect to its probative value in determination of the facts?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did not attach any great importance to it because it -- written in this form, dates in this form, is not a serious business. We can't see which -- it's sloppy work.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should just like to draw attention to the Trial Chamber that the translation of the words are also contested in the one-but-last line of the document, which refers to the interpretation of the statement -- of the status of General Zivanovic, and the Defence would like to ask the interpretation service to give an official explanation as to the word best suited to the original and what it incorporates, what the term comprises.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may, I don't know what it is in the English version, but the usual phrase, the customary phrase that is used in documents on the handing over and takeover of duty, the transfer of duty, is to use in Serbian the word hitherto, "dosadasnji." Dosadasnji commander and the new commander. "Dosadasnji" is the Serbian word, but that word does not mean that at the time the document was issued, compiled and issued, that that dosadasnji commander is no longer the commander. It is a phrase which is always used in documents on the takeover and -- handover and takeover of duty. So this term "dosadasnji," "hitherto" is the accepted term without any arbitration as to who at that point is the commander. It means the outgoing and the one coming in, the one going out and the one coming in. But in standard procedure for correspondence, the term "dosadasnji," "hitherto," is used.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the witness now be given Exhibit 402, please, and it is a report. It is Mr. Butler's report -- no, it is 403, not 402. Exhibit 403 next. And could it be placed on the ELMO, please, showing, focussing on paragraph 7.60, paragraph 7 of that Exhibit, point 60, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, the word "a c'est jour" means -- does it mean that that day is not included? It is a day which is not a day in the life of; it is the day between two days. Which day, no man's land?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It remains the status quo until the transference of duty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Which means he's still in power, he's still in office? Status quo?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So the French word "jusqu'a present" was right, that's what you mean?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here it is falsely -- the demarcation line is false of the handover and takeover. That is to say, when you inaugurate a new commander, when a new commander is inaugurated, and the old commander, the outgoing, the previous commander, is leaving his post or his duties, there is a point -- an act of this transference of duty when they shake hands in front of the assembled gathering, and that is the demarcation line. That is the point from which the new commander takes on all responsibility -- all authority and competency, and the old one loses his authority and competency. So that is the principle. That is the demarcation line or point applied in the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But there is no vacuum? I mean, there is always someone who is General, who is in command at any point. Even in any country where there is a new president coming and the previous one, there is always one who is in power. So --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're quite right. There is no discontinuity of command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And at that time, who would be the commander?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While they're holding hands like this, you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Yes. That day, let's say.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No translation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: We didn't get that answer.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No translation].
